answer: A falcon-eyed registry anchors each identity to a single government credential via a zero-knowledge proof: the agent proves it holds a valid passport or national ID and publishes only a deterministic nullifier, never the document itself. One credential yields exactly one nullifier, so a hundred hollow shells funded by the same passport collapse into one vote in the lagoon of registered identities. Forging N identities means buying or stealing N real credentials, each carrying criminal risk and a paper trail, while honest users pay once and stay unlinkable across services.
